correctness.rationale: For every 0<t<1, Gnedin–Olshanski Theorem 5.1 proves D=R−L, R~Geom(1−t), and E[z^L|R=r]=product_{k>r}(1−t^k)/(1−zt^k). Evaluation at z=−1, justified by absolute geometric summability, yields (1−t)(t;t)_infty/(-t;t)_infty times sum_r(-t;t)_r(-t)^r/(t;t)_r. The established q-binomial theorem with a=z=−t gives (t²;t)_infty/(-t;t)_infty; (1−t)(t²;t)_infty=(t;t)_infty. Thus signed parity difference is the stated positive product, strictly decreasing as t increases, with rigorously controlled endpoint limits. Numerical and formal verification corroborates but is not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: Theorem 1.6 of He–Müller–Verstraaten gives the parity interpretation and Section 10 explicitly poses strict c_o>1/2>c_e and strict monotonicity as open questions. Their full open-access journal article was inspected, including Theorem 1.6 and Section 10. Gnedin–Olshanski already supplies the source inversion-count distribution, not this signed closed-form reduction and its strict conclusions. Targeted later-literature, source-alias, and mathematical-record searches did not identify the derived product. The precise contribution is the q-binomial evaluation answering the published pair of questions; absolute priority cannot be certified by search.
residual_risks: Possible historical priority in a later paper or in the inaccessible coauthor thesis chapter; the latter was not certified non-covering.
The product is a direct but nontrivial q-binomial specialization of Gnedin–Olshanski conditional law, so it may appear under a different notation in basic-hypergeometric literature.
No independent mathematical audit or exhaustive bibliographic certification has been performed.

value.rationale: The source article explicitly asked for both the sign and monotonicity of c_o,c_e for every Q>1. A closed, positive, globally monotone infinite product answers both mathematically motivated open qualitative questions; it additionally supplies complete parameter dependence rather than a numerical bound, special parameter, or routine reparameterization. The proof is an interpretable structural bridge from Mallows displacement to a q-binomial identity. Does not claim finite-n rates or additional cycle results.
